_note: Starting points for the information manager, not transcriptions of any regulator's rules. Everything here is a prototype default (💭).

presets.name: Commonwealth agency
presets.description: Australian Government agency under the Archives Act. Risk-tiered capture: keep more evidence the more a decision relies on AI.
guidance: NAA: AI-generated content is a record; capture is risk-tiered
PROV-style human oversight of checks and disposal (prototype default)

document_types.name: Decision letter or assessment
document_types.description: Informs or records a decision about a person, case or money.

document_types.name: Case note
document_types.description: Working record on a case file.

document_types.name: Briefing or policy paper
document_types.description: Advice to decision-makers; cites research and policy.

document_types.name: Correspondence
document_types.description: Letters and emails to the public.

presets.name: State or territory agency
presets.description: State public sector body. Same tiering, with the NSW-style rule that AI metadata must stay linked to the record.
guidance: State records authority: AI output used in business is a record
NSW-style AI metadata rule: say AI made it, which software, which prompts and inputs
Human oversight of checks and disposal

presets.name: Health service
presets.description: Hospital or clinic using AI scribes and summaries. Clinical notes are decision-informing by default.
guidance: AI scribe output is part of the clinical record once relied on

document_types.name: Clinical note or AI scribe summary
document_types.description: Summary of a consultation written or drafted by AI.

presets.name: Local council
presets.description: Small records team, planning decisions, FOI exposure. Lighter bar on working notes, strict on decisions.
guidance: State records authority rules apply to councils
Planning and FOI records must be retrievable with their AI metadata
